newsitem.title: USA: McDermott sees Q2 shr worse than Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: McDermott sees Q2 shr worse than Q1 loss.

text.p: McDermott International Inc said on Monday that it expected its operating results for the second quarter to be worse than the first quarter $0.18 per share loss, due to ongoing problems at its engineering and construction and power generation business.

The company also said James Dutt, chairman and chief executive officer, would recommend to the board at its November 7 meeting that the quarterly dividend be decreased to $0.05 a share from $0.25 a share.

McDermott's engineering and construction business and its power generation business both continued to suffer from a lack of volume and the power generation business performed poorly on some contracts, a company spokesman said. He said these problems also existed in the first quarter.
The First Call mean estimate for the second quarter was a profit of $0.20 per share.

But McDermott said it was implementing a series of steps including job cuts and the disposal of non-core businesses to improve its financial and operating performance, which would result in after-tax savings of an estimated $50 million.
Dutt said cost reduction efforts would be wide-ranging, from considering the sale of corporate aircraft to the previously announced reorganization of McDermott's global marketing division.

"McDermott is in a period of intense renewal, where everything is being put under close scrutiny," he said. "If we find something doesn't add value, and positive results can't quickly be achieved, we will dispose of it."
McDermott said core businesses included the power generation and government operations of its Babcock & Wilcox unit and the marine construction operations.
The majority-owned J. Ray McDermott subsidiary ran the marine construction business and the company said it had no current intention of changing its ownership of the unit.

McDermott said it would continue to cut personnel and rationalize manufacturing overcapacity at its Babcock & Wilcox power generation group. Since September 1, the company said it had laid off 230 employees.
The company said it would also continue to reduce personnel and other costs at the operating and corporate headquarters of McDermott and J. Ray McDermott.
As part of its marketing reorganization, McDermott said it would close three of its five overseas offices, reduce staff and reassign the marketing function to the operating units.
The company also said it hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles, which started a search to permanently fill the position of chairman and chief executive officer.
